summary: SSE 'shadow frames' after proxy handoff merge consecutive responses into single stitched paragraph
description: Customer reports SSE conversation responses occasionally concatenating two separate turns into one merged paragraph after an upstream proxy connection handoff. The stitched output looks like two answers run together with missing delimiter tokens and duplicated leading white-space. Issue is intermittent and correlated with short edge-proxy reconnects and multiplexed client sessions.
impact: Several customer sessions show merged sentences and duplicated leading fragments instead of two distinct messages. This breaks downstream parsing for NoteStack's automated summarizer and causes user-visible content corruption. Approximately 4% of streaming sessions from this customer's dedicated pool observed within the incident window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure two browser tabs to open multiplexed SSE streams against the same API key with X-Stream-Context header set to 'client-1' and 'client-2' respectively.
2) Send independent prompts that produce multi-paragraph responses in each tab.
3) Trigger a short proxy handoff (simulate TCP teardown) on the client-side path (we reproduced with a synthetic NAT rebind).
4) Observe that, in some runs, the second tab receives the tail of the first tab's final paragraph prepended to its own response, with no terminal event between them.
5) Reproduce more reliably by adding bursty requests and enabling HTTP/2->HTTP/1 bridge at the edge (see environment).

investigation_notes: Initial repro in staging required HTTP/2 multiplexing and an HTTP/2->HTTP/1 bridge at the edge (nginx configured as h2 proxy).

Root cause: race during connection handoff between edge proxy and gateway where worker's outbox drain did not re-check current session binding before writing remaining buffered frames. The old frames retained a Stream-Context header that was not validated end-to-end at the gateway layer.
Frames were small SSE chunks; due to buffered write coalescing the tail of session A could be written into the new socket that had been associated with session B after proxy NAT rebind.
We observed the condition most frequently under high-concurrency (burst) workloads and when keepalive resets were frequent (customer NAT timeouts ~20s).
Mitigation validated: gateway-level strict stream id validation and immediate flush+clear of worker outbox during handoff prevents cross-session leakage.
resolution: Deployed gateway-side validation that rejects/strips SSE frames if X-Stream-Context (Stream-ID) does not match active session binding. Also updated serving-runtime drain logic to re-check binding before each buffered write and clear stale buffer on handoff. Customer SDK 1.12.0 sets per-connection unique stream IDs by default; customer validated fix for 72h. Follow-up: implement improved metrics to detect same-frame-origin anomalies (tracked in INT-1442).
follow_up_actions: Hardening test that simulates NAT rebind+HTTP2 multiplexing in CI
